2610.13797.title: REFLECT: Role-Aware Detection of Sentiment, Emotion, Politeness, and Formality
2610.13797.paper_summary: Detecting communicative meaning in dialogue requires modeling not only lexical content but also the participant-role structures through which sentiment, emotion, politeness, and formality (SEPF) are expressed. Existing approaches rely on contextual language representations while leaving semantic roles implicit. We introduce a role-aware transformer architecture that maps the four SEPF dimensions to theory-grounded Semantic Role Labeling (SRL) configurations, incorporating these configurations directly into the transformer's self-attention mechanism. Role-aware attention models non-directional internal states (sentiment and emotion), while directional role-aware attention captures initiator-to-recipient relations for external cues (politeness and formality). The resulting role-aware representations are fused with contextual embeddings through a learned gate that adaptively weights how much role information each input contributes, rather than appending semantic roles as an auxiliary feature vector. Across four benchmark datasets, the framework yields statistically reliable gains over strong BERT-based baselines for emotion, politeness, and formality, with gains concentrated in theoretically predicted cases such as low-frequency, complex emotions and highly polite expressions; sentiment improvements are marginal and non-significant, suggesting that sentiment is conveyed more through lexical choice than participant-role structure. Additional evaluation on real-world data demonstrates that the framework improves both predictive performance and model traceability. These results demonstrate that linguistically grounded modifications to transformer self-attention improve the detection of communicative meaning, generalize beyond benchmark datasets to real-world mental-health data, and yield traceable, role-grounded explanations that extend beyond predictive performance to interpretability.
2610.13797.paper_summary_zh: 偵測對話中的交際意義不僅需要建模詞彙內容，還需要建模參與者角色結構，通過這些結構表達情感、情緒、禮貌和正式性（SEPF）。現有的方法依賴於上下文語言表示，同時將語義角色隱含化。我們引入了一種角色感知的Transformer架構，將四個 SEPF 維度映射到理論基礎的語義角色標註（SRL）配置，並將這些配置直接納入Transformer的自注意力機制中。角色感知的注意力模型處理非方向性內部狀態（情感和情緒），而方向性角色感知注意力則捕捉發起者到接收者的關係，以獲取外部線索（禮貌和正式性）。所得到的角色感知表示通過一個學習門控與上下文嵌入融合，該門控自適應地加權每個輸入所貢獻的角色信息，而不是將語義角色附加為輔助特徵向量。在四個基準數據集上，該框架在情緒、禮貌和正式性方面相對於強大的基於 BERT 的基準模型產生了統計上可靠的增益，增益集中在理論預測的情況下，如低頻率、複雜情緒和高度禮貌的表達；情感的改善是邊際的且不顯著，這表明情感更多地通過詞彙選擇而非參與者角色結構來傳達。對現實世界數據的額外評估顯示，該框架改善了預測性能和模型可追溯性。這些結果表明，基於語言的變更對Transformer自注意力的改進提高了交際意義的檢測，超越基準數據集推廣到現實世界的心理健康數據，並產生可追溯的、基於角色的解釋，這些解釋超越了預測性能達到可解釋性。
